page: Amazon Web Services g6f.2xlarge is an accelerated computing virtual machine provisioned on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance features an AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, supplying 8 vCPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading. It incorporates 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a fractional partition of an NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU, configured with 0.25 of the GPU unit and 6 GB of total VRAM. Storage includes a 200 GB local NVMe SSD, and networking performance features a 5 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-core CPU execution, achieving a top 25% ranking in stress-ng at 2974.28, alongside a multi-core score of 11911.31 in the middle tier. In LLM benchmarks, the hardware demonstrates high-tier prompt processing throughput for medium 7B models at 528.61 tokens per second, placing it in the top 10%, alongside 11.84 tokens per second in text generation. Read and write memory bandwidth for large uncached 256MB blocks registers in the lower 25% at 37.94 GB/sec and 22.42 GB/sec respectively, reflecting the throughput characteristics of DDR4 relative to newer architectures.

The fractional NVIDIA L4 deployment provides qualitative efficiency by enabling access to modern Ada Lovelace graphics and AI acceleration without requiring full GPU allocation. While large models exceeding the 6 GB VRAM envelope are unsuitable, the platform fits targeted workloads including medium-sized AI inference, real-time graphics rendering, video encoding, and localized caching applications supported by its direct-attached NVMe storage.

It integrates 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, a 200 GB local NVMe SSD, and a 5 Gbps baseline network interface. GPU acceleration is delivered by a 0.25 partition of an NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU equipped with 6 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results show strong single-core compute performance and top-tier prompt processing speeds for 7B parameter models at 528.61 tokens per second, though large-block memory bandwidth is comparatively constrained. Balancing fractional GPU resources and local fast storage, this instance fits lightweight machine learning inference, real-time computer graphics, video transcoding, and web applications needing modest hardware acceleration.
